doc.title: Sherrie Maricle interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]

title: How Maricle describes herself: musician with many roles
summary: Monk Rowe asks how to introduce her; she says she does many things and wonders whether focusing on one would have taken her further.

story.theme_name: Opening the interview: Monk Rowe's welcome and archive boilerplate
story.community_name: Opening the Hamilton College interview: introductions and boilerplate

blocks.x: We are in Clearwater Beach at the Arbors Jazz Fest and my name is Monk Rowe. I’m very pleased to have Sherrie Maricle with me today. And usually I say saxophonist somebody or, you know, keyboardist, but I’m not sure which to go first with you. I was looking at your write-up and I don’t know how you handle your life.
I was hoping you could tell me how I should identify myself. That’s been my problem all along.

Yeah. I have a lot of different things that I do. And every time I look back on my career I wonder if — it’s always been really interesting to me and I think kept me motivated, highly motivated, about music in general. But then sometimes I wonder well if I would have just picked one thing would I have excelled to a higher level. And I don’t know if I would have or not. I’m not sure.
Because the way it is now it’s just, every day is a thrill to be a musician.
